test_cases.prompt: Resume make-literature-note in an existing vault with a Resource and a Literature note but no cache; the note has legacy Key Claims and selective concepts.
test_cases.expected_output: Builds the source map from the complete Resource first, never from selective Literature content, reconciles Core Idea, Key Claims/Source Points, Key Concepts, Mentioned, and Open Questions to source units with matched, matched-with-qualification-risk, matched-to-multiple-units, unmatched, or source-support-unclear statuses, and does not rewrite semantics automatically.

assertions.text: build the cache from the Literature note

test_cases.prompt: A Literature note's Resource is missing while resuming existing work.
test_cases.expected_output: Stops source-first reconciliation, reports the missing Resource as a blocker, and preserves the existing note unchanged.

test_cases.prompt: Use files fixtures/lazy-migration-note.md and fixtures/lazy-migration-unrelated.md with config migrations.literature_headings.mode=lazy. Access only lazy-migration-note.md.
test_cases.expected_output: On first access, stages only lazy-migration-note.md, renames its exact ## Key Claims heading to ## Source Points, validates and publishes through /using-slipbox CAS, and leaves lazy-migration-unrelated.md byte-for-byte unchanged.

test_cases.prompt: Start or resume Literature work for a Resource with explicit inquiry context, implied reflection, no stated purpose, and exploratory intent; the Resource is a news report containing an allegation attributed to a secondary source. The user may be Confident, Hesitant, Blank, or Confused, and may treat the Resource as primary or secondary regardless of its type.
test_cases.expected_output: Uses /using-slipbox to start or resume recoverable work, loads or builds the source cache, creates a session-scoped inquiry map, and derives the grounding frontier at runtime. Follows one substantive question at a time and dispatches all four reading states (Confident, Hesitant, Blank, Confused) without a universal opener. Keeps primary/secondary posture independent of Resource type and preserves the news allegation's attribution and uncertainty.

test_cases.prompt: Ground one sharp inquiry-central Source Point and several supporting/contextual points, including a consequential ambiguous point, then pause and resume the Literature session.
test_cases.expected_output: Applies the Adaptive Split Gate: inquiry-central work asks the user for a semantic relation before drafting; supporting/contextual work may be agent-drafted; consequential or ambiguous work is verified against the source without forced paraphrase. Checkpoints the inquiry map and staged draft through /using-slipbox, never mutates the final literature path mid-session, and on resume reuses prior comprehension evidence to continue at the next unresolved obligation.

test_cases.prompt: A Literature session has Blank or not-started reading with a source. The user first considers reading alone, then chooses to work through the source collaboratively.
test_cases.expected_output: Offers the choice between reading alone and collaboration. If the user reads alone, pauses without dispatching guided reading; if the user chooses collaboration, dispatches guided reading and continues one substantive question at a time.

test_cases.prompt: The user identifies a fidelity error in a previously published Source Point and supplies corrected wording while another process may have changed the final note.
test_cases.expected_output: Stages the correction in the explicit <staged-draft> path, validates that staged artifact, and publishes through /using-slipbox with compare-and-swap against the expected final-file fingerprint. A concurrent change stops recovery and never overwrites the final path directly; after successful publication, validates the saved path.

test_cases.prompt: Build a source map and inquiry map for a conceptual source with several argument moves and uneven user relevance.
test_cases.expected_output: Keeps the reusable source map source-owned and separate from reader inquiry or transcript; references source-unit IDs from the inquiry map; derives a grounding frontier at runtime rather than storing an authoritative queue. Routes high-learning/low-risk work through a user semantic relation before the agent drafts, while low-learning/high-risk work is verified against the source without forcing paraphrase.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note from resources/2026-08-08-design-tokens.md, a freshly clipped source with no literature note yet
test_cases.expected_output: Loads or builds source-owned analysis, creates a session-scoped inquiry map, and derives the grounding frontier at runtime without persisting a queue. Runs one continuous conversation with one substantive question at a time. Uses the Adaptive Split Gate: inquiry-central points require semantic reconstruction, while supporting/contextual points may be agent-drafted and source-verified. Stages each point through /using-slipbox and publishes only after final validation.

test_cases.prompt: make-literature-note on resources/2026-08-08-design-tokens.md, where the literature note already has one confirmed claim from a prior session
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the existing literature note's ### Source Point headings first, excludes covered units from the derived frontier, and does not re-write the Core Idea line.

test_cases.prompt: make-literature-note, invoked bare with no argument, but a resource was just clipped moments earlier in the same conversation
test_cases.expected_output: Infers the source from the just-clipped resource rather than asking the user to name it again.

test_cases.prompt: make-literature-note, invoked bare with no argument and nothing inferrable from context
test_cases.expected_output: Asks the user which source to ground rather than guessing.

test_cases.prompt: make-literature-note on a source, and the conversation winds down naturally with two backlog candidates never mentioned
test_cases.expected_output: Nudges once for the untouched candidates ('you haven't mentioned X - is that not something the source argues, or should we leave it?'), but if the user says 'I think that's everything,' ends the sitting regardless of what the backlog still shows uncovered.

test_cases.prompt: make-literature-note on a candidate whose derived filename already exists on disk with unrelated content
test_cases.expected_output: Stops and asks the user to reword the claim or confirm a genuine duplicate, rather than auto-disambiguating the filename.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note on fixtures/sun-gating-and-morning-light.md, using fixtures/sun-gating-grounding-transcript.md as the session transcript, where the user notices mid-session that the source never actually settles whether indoor light exposure can substitute for outdoor light on a cloudy day
test_cases.expected_output: Captures the gap as a bullet in a top-level '## Open Questions' section, sibling to '## Source Points', in plain declarative form naming what the source leaves unclear. Does not invent the open question itself or add one unprompted. If the user then offers their own guess at an answer, nests it as an '*Assumption*' bullet under that question, marked as the user's own guess, never written into a Source Point.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note on fixtures/less-is-more.md, continuing a session where the user has already confirmed several claims that all rest on the same understanding/judgment-determines-what-to-keep move across different domains, plus four claims each promoting one item off the source's own single seven-bullet list
test_cases.expected_output: At the natural close of the session ('Knowing when the session is done'), flags the cross-claim overlap and checks the confirmed count against the 6-8 reference point rather than staying silent, and treats the four list-derived claims as one claim citing the list as a whole with its items folded into Evidence rather than one claim per item — never interrupting mid-claim to enforce this, only at the session-close sweep.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note on fixtures/less-is-more.md, at the point in the session where the first claim is about to be drafted and the Core Idea line has not yet been written
test_cases.expected_output: Before showing any drafted Core Idea, asks a genuine open question first ('what do you think is the main idea this source is arguing?') rather than presenting a finished synthesis for a nod. Drafts the Core Idea silently at the first claim as before, but confirmation of it is deferred to the same 'Knowing when the session is done' pause used for density, and that confirmation is itself an open question, never a binary yes/no.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note on fixtures/sun-gating-and-morning-light.md, using fixtures/sun-gating-grounding-transcript.md, where the source states the body is 'most sensitive to light' in the first 30-60 minutes and the user's restatement drifts toward calling that window 'most effective for setting the circadian clock'
test_cases.expected_output: The Conclusion-review check catches the epistemic-stance upgrade — a stated fact ('most sensitive') being strengthened into an unstated comparative-efficacy conclusion ('most effective') the source never makes — and holds the claim to the source's actual hedge/fact rather than letting the stronger wording through.

assertions.text: most effective for setting the circadian clock

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note from a Resource whose exact source title is 'Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever: Matt Pocock', with filenames.literature configured as Sentence case and prefixes.literature configured as '§'
test_cases.expected_output: Writes the Literature H1 with the exact Resource title, and derives the complete basename through `slipbox filename format`, yielding `§ Software fundamentals matter more than ever: Matt Pocock` while preserving the proper-name span and subtitle colon.

assertions.text: # Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever: Matt Pocock
# § Software Fundamentals Matter More Than Ever: Matt Pocock
§ Software fundamentals matter more than ever: Matt Pocock

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note from a Resource titled 'API Design for NASA Teams', with filenames.literature configured as Sentence case
test_cases.expected_output: Preserves the exact source-title H1 and derives `§ API design for NASA teams`, retaining both acronyms while lowercasing ordinary words.

test_cases.prompt: /make-literature-note closes after several confirmed claims
test_cases.expected_output: Audits every retained Source Point against its source unit for fidelity, posture, attribution, scope, certainty, and ambiguity. Uses targeted integrity checks rather than an exhaustive universal source-to-note audit; material changes re-audit affected points before staged publication.

test_cases.prompt: The user declines a valid source-audit finding and asks to finish
test_cases.expected_output: Reports the literature note as deliberately partial after the user declined the valid finding, discards the session inquiry assessment, and does not persist a grounding frontier unless explicitly requested.

test_cases.prompt: A confirmed claim introduces a method, a named tool, a book, and an event
test_cases.expected_output: Adds abstract methods/frameworks to Key Concepts and concrete named books, tools, and events to Mentioned during staged point assembly, then performs one final batch pass before reaction and staged-artifact validation.

test_cases.prompt: The session is ready to finish
test_cases.expected_output: Follows the fixed order: convergent source audit, density merge and re-audit if changed, final Core Idea, final Key Concepts/Mentioned batch, reaction and optional Evergreen routing, then final artifact validation. Done cannot fire early.

test_cases.prompt: A source reports that a clinician recommends morning light, while the source itself does not endorse or quantify that recommendation; write the literature note Source Point.
test_cases.expected_output: Preserves reporting posture and attribution (the source reports the clinician's recommendation), keeps certainty and scope unchanged, and does not rewrite it as the source's own explanatory or causal claim.

test_cases.prompt: The conversation drafted a clinical light-therapy claim, parked it for later, and also has one untouched source argument; the user says, 'I think that's everything.'
test_cases.expected_output: Keeps the drafted-but-unconfirmed item distinct from the untouched item, names the drafted item specifically, gives the untouched item one nudge, and ends when the user says they are finished. It does not treat either item as Covered or collapse the drafted state into Untouched.

test_cases.prompt: The source-shaped closeout finds an optional related idea, but the user declines it and asks to finish.
test_cases.expected_output: Treats the optional discovery as a clean boundary, not a partial note; discards the session inquiry assessment and completes the retained note.

test_cases.prompt: At closeout, a retained Source Point upgrades a hedge and reverses chronology, while another source proposition was never captured.
test_cases.expected_output: Runs a targeted audit for attribution, certainty, scope, chronology, causality, reported-versus-verified status, speaker, analysis-versus-observation, and dispute. Flags the distortion and qualification drift, but does not require an exhaustive universal source-to-note audit of every uncaptured proposition.

test_cases.prompt: The final Core Idea was drafted silently at the first claim; at closeout the user reconstructs the source's throughline, then responds to the current Core Idea wording.
test_cases.expected_output: Uses the user's reconstruction as the active-learning moment, then verifies the current Core Idea through an open confirmation question and rewrites it only if the reconstruction differs.

assertions.text: what do you think is the main idea
how would you put it now

test_cases.prompt: A literature note closes with Core Idea, three retained Source Points, one Open Question, and one discussed claim parked for later.
test_cases.expected_output: Gives a compact structural closeout listing the Core Idea, all three retained Source Point headings, the Open Question, the unresolved parked item, and the saved path; shows the full note only on request.

test_cases.prompt: A factual source-grounding session reaches closeout with no user reflection or opinion.
test_cases.expected_output: Omits the reaction prompt for the factual session and proceeds to final validation without asking what the user thinks of the article.

assertions.text: what do you think of this article

test_cases.prompt: During the final concepts batch, the user adds a relevant named tool that was not surfaced in the retained-point support.
test_cases.expected_output: Accepts the explicit user addition into Mentioned, while keeping the candidate union bounded to retained-point support, source-present inquiry relevance, and explicit additions; it does not scan unrelated source-map candidates.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: a short essay with one clear thesis and two supporting reasons is passed to /make-literature-note.
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the complete Resource, asks the user to reconstruct the thesis and its relation to the reasons, records the confirmed thesis as the Core Idea and the supported reasons as Source Points, then stages and validates the Literature note before publication.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: a Wikipedia-like explanation defines a concept, gives historical context, and notes a limitation; ground it with /make-literature-note.
test_cases.expected_output: Separates definition, context, and limitation into source units, preserves explanatory scope and qualification, and uses the Adaptive Split Gate so inquiry-central work is reconstructed by the user while context is source-verified.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: breaking news reports an allegation attributed to a former contractor, includes that contractor's denial, and leaves verification pending.
test_cases.expected_output: Preserves attribution, denial, uncertainty, chronology, and reported-versus-verified status, and never rewrites the allegation as an established fact.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: an explanatory lecture walks through a mechanism, then gives a practical example and a caveat; the user chooses collaborative reading.
test_cases.expected_output: Dispatches guided reading only after the collaborative choice, asks one substantive question at a time, and consolidates the mechanism, example, and caveat through one open Gate before staging Source Points.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: a mixed investigation combines direct observations, a paraphrased expert interpretation, competing hypotheses, and unresolved evidence.
test_cases.expected_output: Maps observations, attributed interpretation, hypotheses, and unresolved evidence separately; preserves speaker, analysis-versus-observation, dispute, and certainty; and records unresolved gaps as Open Questions.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: resume a partially read source after an interrupted Literature session with a checkpointed inquiry map and staged Source Point.
test_cases.expected_output: Uses /using-slipbox to verify fingerprints, reuses prior comprehension evidence and the staged draft, skips resolved obligations, and resumes at the next unresolved thinking obligation without repeating the interview.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: resume an existing legacy Literature note with ## Key Claims and no source cache, while the Resource is available and migration policy is defer.
test_cases.expected_output: Reads the complete Resource first, builds source-owned analysis, reconciles legacy content privately, leaves the final note unchanged under defer, and reports source-support-unclear items without rewriting semantics automatically.

test_cases.prompt: End-to-end fixture: close a grounded Literature note whose confirmed Source Point introduces a relevant named framework that the user wants to develop immediately as a Reference note.
test_cases.expected_output: Completes Literature closeout first, adds the framework to Key Concepts, offers the context-aware Reference handoff only after the Literature artifact is validated and saved, and passes grounded source identity forward without rerunning Literature work.
